comments.author: @robertstanfill2360
comments.text: I was always taught there were no horses in the Americas until the Spaniards came after Columbus. Was that in correct? Just asking.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Mostly right, with a wrinkle - horses actually originated in North America millions of years ago but went extinct there around 10,000 years ago, likely tied to the end of the last ice age. So there's truth to both: horses were gone from the Americas for thousands of years, and it was the Spanish who reintroduced them in the 1500s.

comments.author: @World_Untold_321
comments.text: Having worked in global freight for a few years, watching ships queue up outside the canal during the drought was nerve-wracking. We had containers stranded for weeks, and the auction prices for transit slots got completely insane. Great video explaining why this narrow strip of water holds so much of the global economy hostage!

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That's a genuinely valuable ground-level view - the auction prices for transit slots during the drought became a real case study in just how much leverage this one strip of water holds over global trade.
